title: Overheating, loud fans, and thermal throttling
summary: The computer generates excessive heat, causes cooling fans to run at maximum speed continuously, or shuts down to protect components.
symptoms: Case fans scream at maximum RPM even while sitting on the desktop
Laptop chassis or desktop case feels uncomfortably hot to the touch
Sudden frame drops and stuttering in games after 10-15 minutes of play

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Check hardware temperatures with HWiNFO64
fix_steps.detail: Download HWiNFO64 (Sensors only mode). Check CPU Tctl/Tdie, GPU Core, and GPU Hotspot temperatures. Temperatures exceeding 95°C on CPU or 105°C on GPU Hotspot indicate thermal throttling.

fix_steps.title: Clean dust out of intake filters and heatsink fins
fix_steps.detail: Use compressed air or an electric duster to blow dust out of radiator fins, GPU heatsinks, and mesh case filters. Hold fan blades still so they don't overspin.

fix_steps.title: Repaste CPU and GPU with high-grade thermal paste
fix_steps.detail: Wipe dried paste using isopropyl alcohol (90%+) and apply fresh compound (Noctua NT-H2, Arctic MX-6, or Thermal Grizzly) with even cross-pattern mounting pressure.

fix_steps.title: Adjust fan curves in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Enter BIOS setup → Q-Fan / Hardware Monitor. Verify fan headers are set to PWM mode (for 4-pin fans) and create a progressive curve hitting 100% fan speed at 85°C.

title: CPU reaches 100°C+ and triggers emergency thermal shutdown
summary: The central processor hits its maximum junction temperature (TjMax 100-105°C) and cuts power instantly to prevent silicon damage.
symptoms: PC abruptly shuts off with no blue screen during gaming or video rendering
System refuses to power back on for 2-3 minutes until the CPU cools down
BIOS warning on next boot: 'CPU Over Temperature Error!'

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Verify CPU cooler fan and pump are running
fix_steps.detail: Look inside the chassis when powering on. Ensure CPU cooler fans are spinning. If using an AIO liquid cooler, place two fingers on the pump block to feel for vibration.

fix_steps.title: Inspect cooler mounting pressure and bracket alignment
fix_steps.detail: Remove the cooler. Ensure all four mounting standoffs are fully threaded and tension screws are tightened diagonally in an X-pattern until they bottom out.

fix_steps.title: Remove factory plastic protective peel sticker
fix_steps.detail: Check the copper contact base of the heatsink. Leaving the transparent 'Warning: Remove before installation' film intact is the most common reason for 100°C temperatures on new builds.

fix_steps.title: Disable aggressive motherboard overclocking defaults
fix_steps.detail: In BIOS, turn off 'Multi-Core Enhancement' (ASUS), 'Enhanced Turbo' (MSI), or set Intel baseline power limits (PL1=125W, PL2=253W) to prevent dangerous over-volting.

title: AIO liquid cooler pump failure (immediate 95°C at idle)
summary: The mechanical pump impeller has seized or lost electrical power, causing zero coolant flow and thermal saturation within 60 seconds of turning on.
symptoms: CPU immediately spikes to 90-100°C inside BIOS within 60 seconds of powering on
One AIO tube is scalding hot while the other tube and radiator remain cold
BIOS reports CPU_FAN or AIO_PUMP RPM as 0 or 'N/A'

fix_steps.title: Check pump power connection (SATA and 4-pin header)
fix_steps.detail: Verify the AIO pump connector is firmly plugged into the dedicated 'AIO_PUMP' or 'W_PUMP' motherboard header, and auxiliary SATA power cables from the PSU are latched.

fix_steps.title: Set pump header to 100% Full Speed in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Liquid cooling pumps require a constant 12V supply. In BIOS Fan Control, ensure the AIO_PUMP header is set to 100% constant speed, not fluctuating with CPU temperature.

fix_steps.title: Listen and feel for pump motor vibrations
fix_steps.detail: Place a hand on the CPU block. If you feel no vibration and hear silence or a faint electrical clicking/rattling noise, the pump motor has burned out.

fix_steps.title: Dislodge air bubble airlock in pump chamber
fix_steps.detail: Ensure the radiator is mounted higher than the pump block. If the pump is the highest point in the loop, air collects in the pump. Tip case 45 degrees while running to dislodge bubbles.

title: Transparent warning sticker left on cooler copper plate
summary: The factory protective plastic film was left adhering to the copper heatsink base, acting as a thermal insulator between the CPU and cooler.
symptoms: Brand new PC build reaches 90°C on desktop with 3% CPU usage
Fans run at 100% maximum speed constantly from the very first boot
Cooler radiator or heatsink fins feel completely cold to the touch

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Dismount CPU cooler block
fix_steps.detail: Unscrew the four mounting thumb-screws diagonally and gently twist the cooler block slightly left and right to break thermal paste vacuum, then carefully lift it off the CPU.

fix_steps.title: Peel off the transparent plastic film
fix_steps.detail: Locate the clear plastic film on the copper coldplate with the text 'WARNING: PEEL OFF BEFORE INSTALLING' and peel it completely away.

fix_steps.title: Clean thermal paste residue with isopropyl alcohol
fix_steps.detail: Wipe off all existing thermal paste from both the CPU heat spreader and cooler base using 90%+ isopropyl alcohol and lint-free wipes.

fix_steps.title: Apply fresh thermal compound and remount
fix_steps.detail: Place a pea-sized dot or an X-pattern of fresh thermal paste on the center of the CPU and securely fasten the cooler screws evenly.

title: High GPU hotspot delta (>30°C difference between core and hotspot)
summary: Thermal paste pump-out or uneven mounting bracket pressure causes the GPU hotspot (junction) to hit 105°C+ while the core reports a deceptive 65°C.
symptoms: GPU fans suddenly ramp to 100% (jet engine sound) during gaming
HWiNFO shows GPU Temperature at 68°C but GPU Hot Spot at 105-110°C
Graphics card downclocks heavily and framerates stutter

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Check GPU core-to-hotspot temperature delta
fix_steps.detail: Open HWiNFO64. Under GPU sensors, subtract GPU Core from GPU Hot Spot. A delta above 20-25°C indicates paste degradation or uneven heatsink contact.

fix_steps.title: Repaste GPU with viscous paste or PTM7950 phase-change pad
fix_steps.detail: Direct-die GPU silicon causes standard paste to pump out under thermal cycling. Use high-viscosity paste (Thermalright TFX, Kingpin KPx) or Honeywell PTM7950 phase-change pad.

fix_steps.title: Tighten GPU retention bracket spring screws
fix_steps.detail: Tighten the 4 spring-loaded cross-bracket screws behind the GPU core in an X-pattern to ensure firm, balanced mounting pressure across the die.

fix_steps.title: Ensure thermal putty or pads on VRAM are correct thickness
fix_steps.detail: If thermal pads on VRAM are even 0.5mm too thick, they will prevent the copper base from contacting the GPU die.

title: Heatsink fin stacks and mesh filters choked with dust
summary: Dense lint and dust blankets the spaces between radiator fins, blocking airflow and trapping convection heat inside the chassis.
symptoms: Exhaust fans blow lukewarm or cold air despite high hardware temperatures
PC was quiet when bought 2 years ago, but now sounds like a hair dryer
Visible grey lint layer covering front intake mesh and fan blades

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Power down and clean dust filters
fix_steps.detail: Remove magnetic or slide-out dust filters from the front, top, and bottom PSU intake of the case. Wash with warm water or vacuum thoroughly and dry completely.

fix_steps.title: Blow compressed air through heatsink fins from inside out
fix_steps.detail: Use a can of compressed air or electric air duster. Blow air in the opposite direction of normal airflow to eject compacted lint mats out of the radiator. SAFETY: Hold the fan blades still with a finger or non-conductive tool while spraying compressed air. Allowing fans to free-spin rapidly can burn out bearings and generate reverse voltage back into the motherboard fan header.

fix_steps.title: Hold fan blades still while blowing air
fix_steps.detail: Always hold the center fan hub with a finger or pencil. Allowing high-pressure air to free-spin fan blades generates reverse voltage (back-EMF) that can burn motherboard fan headers.

fix_steps.title: Clean fan blade leading edges with isopropyl alcohol
fix_steps.detail: Wipe sticky dust crust off fan blades to reduce aerodynamic noise and restore factory cubic feet per minute (CFM) airflow.

title: Aged, dried, or cracked thermal interface material (TIM)
summary: Thermal paste degrades and turns into dry chalk after 3-5 years of thermal expansion and contraction, creating microscopic air gaps that insulate heat.
symptoms: Gradual temperature increase of 15-20°C over several years of use
Fans ramp to high speed within 5 seconds of opening any application
Cooler was never repasted since original assembly 4+ years ago

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Remove CPU cooler carefully (twist before pulling)
fix_steps.detail: Warm up the CPU with a benchmark before shutdown. Unscrew cooler and gently twist back and forth. Never pull straight up on AMD AM4 CPUs, which can yank the CPU out of the locked socket.

fix_steps.title: Dissolve dried paste using 90%+ isopropyl alcohol
fix_steps.detail: Apply isopropyl alcohol with a paper towel or microfiber cloth. Clean until both the CPU IHS and cooler copper base shine mirror-clean.

fix_steps.title: Apply fresh high-performance thermal paste
fix_steps.detail: Place a pea-sized drop (or an X with 4 corner dots) in the center of the heat spreader. Do not use conductive liquid metal on bare aluminum.

fix_steps.title: Torque mounting screws progressively in cross pattern
fix_steps.detail: Turn screw 1 two rotations, then diagonal screw 2 two rotations, then 3 and 4, repeating until all four spring-loaded screws bottom out firmly.

title: Negative case pressure suffocating graphics card and pulling dust
summary: Case fans are configured with more exhaust than intake (or all fans blowing out), starving the GPU of fresh cool air and sucking dust through unfiltered seams.
symptoms: Removing the case tempered glass side panel instantly drops GPU temp by 10-15°C
Dust collects rapidly around PCIe slots and rear panel crevices
GPU intake fans fight against internal case vacuum

fix_steps.title: Check fan flow orientation (Intake vs Exhaust)
fix_steps.detail: Remember the PC rule: 'Air flows towards the cross bracket / sticker'. Ensure front and bottom fans face inward (intake), while rear and top fans blow outward (exhaust).

fix_steps.title: Ensure positive or neutral air pressure balance
fix_steps.detail: Configure intake fans to provide slightly higher CFM than exhaust fans (e.g., 3 front intake fans and 1 rear + 1 top exhaust fan).

fix_steps.title: Remove decorative solid front glass/plastic panels
fix_steps.detail: Cases with solid glass front panels restrict intake airflow to tiny side slits. Upgrade to a mesh front panel or remove front bezel to verify temperature impact.

fix_steps.title: Install bottom intake fans beneath GPU
fix_steps.detail: If your case has bottom PSU shroud fan mounts, install intake fans blowing directly into the GPU cooling fans.

title: Motherboard pushing excessive voltage (ASUS MCE / Gigabyte Enhanced)
summary: Default motherboard firmware disables Intel/AMD factory power limits, pumping upwards of 1.45V into the CPU and generating over 300W of heat.
symptoms: CPU pulls 250W-320W in benchmarks and hits 100°C on a 360mm AIO cooler
CPU Vcore voltages spike above 1.40V in HWiNFO
System crashes in Cinebench or rendering after 30 seconds

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Disable ASUS MultiCore Enhancement / MSI Enhanced Turbo
fix_steps.detail: In BIOS under Ai Tweaker / Overclocking, find 'ASUS MultiCore Enhancement' and change from 'Auto - Enforce All Limits' to 'Disabled - Enforce All Limits'.

fix_steps.title: Apply Intel Baseline / Default Power Profile
fix_steps.detail: Update to the latest BIOS version containing the Intel Default Settings profile. CRITICAL SAFETY: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing to avoid corrupting the motherboard EEPROM. Ensure PL1 (Long Duration) is set to 125W or 253W according to Intel specifications.

fix_steps.title: Apply negative voltage offset (Undervolt)
fix_steps.detail: In BIOS, set CPU Core Voltage mode to 'Offset Mode', select '-', and enter a conservative offset of 0.050V (-50mV) to drop temperatures by 5-10°C with zero performance loss.

fix_steps.title: Configure AMD Precision Boost Overdrive Curve Optimizer
fix_steps.detail: On Ryzen processors, enable PBO Curve Optimizer → All Cores → Negative → start with 15 or 20 for cooler operating temperatures.

title: Improper thermal pad thickness on laptop VRM and VRAM
summary: After cleaning or repasting a gaming laptop, incorrect thermal pad thickness prevents the heatsink from making contact with the CPU/GPU silicon dies.
symptoms: Laptop was running 75°C, but after user repasting immediately hits 100°C on desktop
Laptop shuts down 1 minute into booting any 3D game
Thermal paste on CPU shows zero spread when heatsink is reopened

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Replace solid pads with high-conformability Thermal Putty
fix_steps.detail: Laptops use non-standard pad thicknesses (0.75mm, 1.25mm). Replace stiff silicone pads with moldable thermal putty (Upsiren U6 Pro, ZT-PY6, CX-H98) that compresses perfectly.

fix_steps.title: Check heatsink screw numbering sequence
fix_steps.detail: Laptop vapor chambers have numbered screw brackets (1 through 8). Always tighten in sequential order 1, 2, 3... to prevent the vapor chamber from cocking at an angle.

fix_steps.title: Inspect copper heat pipes for vapor seal rupture
fix_steps.detail: If a copper heat pipe gets bent or punctured, the internal vacuum and distilled water escape, turning the heat pipe into a useless hollow tube.

fix_steps.title: Elevate rear laptop feet by 1 inch
fix_steps.detail: Propping up the back of the laptop with a book or laptop stand provides 30-40% more airflow intake through bottom vents.

title: Motherboard VRM (Voltage Regulator Module) overheating and throttling
summary: An entry-level motherboard lacking VRM heatsinks throttles a high-wattage CPU down to 800MHz because power MOSFETs exceed 115°C.
symptoms: CPU temperatures are fine (60°C), but CPU clock speed suddenly drops to 800MHz during heavy load
HWiNFO reports 'VRM Temperature' or 'Motherboard Temperature 4' above 105°C
Plastic smell emanates from upper left corner of motherboard

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Direct an airflow fan onto the motherboard VRM area
fix_steps.detail: AIO water coolers provide zero airflow over the socket. Position a small 80mm or 120mm fan blowing directly over the naked MOSFETs near the CPU socket.

fix_steps.title: Enforce strict TDP power limits in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: In BIOS, manually set CPU Long Duration Power Limit (PL1) to 65W or 95W so the board's unheatsinked power phases are not overwhelmed.

fix_steps.title: Attach aftermarket adhesive mini heatsinks
fix_steps.detail: Apply small aluminum or copper heatsinks with pre-applied thermal adhesive tape to the bare black square MOSFET chips.

fix_steps.title: Switch from liquid AIO to a top-down air cooler
fix_steps.detail: Top-down air coolers (like Noctua NH-L12S or Thermalright AXP) blow direct exhaust air over the surrounding motherboard VRM capacitors and chokes.

title: Power supply fan failure or stuck in Eco mode
summary: The cooling fan inside the power supply fails to spin under load, causing internal PSU capacitors to overheat and trip over-temperature protection (OTP).
symptoms: PC shuts down instantly without warning during heavy gaming sessions
Top or bottom of the PC chassis above the PSU shroud is burning hot to the touch
Flashlight inspection reveals the PSU fan is completely still even during gaming

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Toggle the PSU Eco / Hybrid / Zero-RPM switch
fix_steps.detail: Many high-end PSUs (EVGA, Seasonic, Corsair) feature a toggle switch on the back for 'Eco Mode' or 'Hybrid Fan'. Flip it OFF to force the fan to spin continuously.

fix_steps.title: Clean dust buildup inside PSU shroud
fix_steps.detail: Use compressed air through the PSU fan grille. (WARNING: Never open a power supply casing; internal capacitors carry lethal electric charges even when unplugged). SAFETY: Hold the fan blades still with a finger or non-conductive tool while spraying compressed air. Allowing fans to free-spin rapidly can burn out bearings and generate reverse voltage back into the motherboard fan header.

fix_steps.title: Verify PSU orientation (fan facing fresh air)
fix_steps.detail: If the PC sits on a desk, ensure the PSU fan faces downward toward the case bottom dust filter (or upward if the case floor is completely solid).

fix_steps.title: Replace the power supply unit
fix_steps.detail: If the PSU fan does not spin when Eco mode is disabled and the unit trips off under load, the internal fan controller or bearing has failed; RMA or replace the PSU.

title: Case or CPU fans running at 100% full speed all the time (DC mode)
summary: 4-pin PWM fans are configured as 3-pin DC (voltage controlled) in BIOS, supplying a constant 12 volts and forcing unbearable fan noise at idle.
symptoms: Fans run at deafening maximum RPM from the second the PC powers on
Fan speed never drops, even when CPU temperature is 30°C
Software fan control tools (Fan Control, SpeedFan) have no effect

fix_steps.title: Enter BIOS setup and open Hardware Monitor / Fan Control
fix_steps.detail: Restart PC and press Del or F2. Navigate to 'Q-Fan Control' (ASUS), 'Hardware Monitor' (MSI), or 'Smart Fan' (Gigabyte).

fix_steps.title: Switch Fan Control Mode from DC to PWM
fix_steps.detail: Select each fan header (CPU_FAN, CHA_FAN1, etc.). Change the control mode from 'DC' (or Auto) to 'PWM'. 4-pin fans require PWM pulse signaling to modulate speed.

fix_steps.title: Run automatic fan tuning calibration
fix_steps.detail: Click 'Fan Tuning' or 'Optimize All' in BIOS. The motherboard tests minimum starting voltages for each fan to prevent stalled fans at low RPM.

fix_steps.title: Use Fan Control (open-source software) in Windows
fix_steps.detail: Download the lightweight, open-source 'Fan Control' utility to bind case fan curves to both CPU and GPU temperatures simultaneously.

title: Desktop placed on thick carpet suffocating power supply intake
summary: Placing a computer case directly on thick carpet blocks the bottom-facing PSU air intake, trapping heat and burning out the power supply.
symptoms: Case bottom is excessively hot
Power supply fan makes strained whirring sound
Random PC reboots under gaming load

fix_steps.title: Elevate the PC off the carpet
fix_steps.detail: Place a rigid wooden board, computer riser stand, or ceramic tile underneath the PC feet to provide at least 1-2 inches of clear clearance below the bottom intake.

fix_steps.title: Remove and wash bottom PSU dust filter
fix_steps.detail: Pull out the sliding mesh filter at the bottom rear of the case and wash out carpet fibers and accumulated dust.

fix_steps.title: Flip PSU orientation if carpet placement is unavoidable
fix_steps.detail: If you must place the PC on carpet and lack a stand, reinstall the PSU with its fan facing upward into the chassis to pull air from inside the case.

fix_steps.title: Inspect PSU bottom intake fan with a flashlight
fix_steps.detail: Ensure carpet fibers have not wrapped around the fan motor axle.

title: PCIe 4.0/5.0 NVMe SSD thermal throttling (transfer speed drops to zero)
summary: High-speed NVMe solid state drive controller chips exceed 85°C during sustained file writes, cutting speeds by 90% to avoid burning flash memory.
symptoms: Large 50GB+ file transfer starts at 5000 MB/s then plunges to 50 MB/s
Games stutter heavily when loading open-world assets
CrystalDiskInfo reports SSD Temperature in bright red warning at 80-90°C

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Install motherboard M.2 aluminum heatsink
fix_steps.detail: PCIe Gen 4 and Gen 5 SSDs require active or passive heatsinks. Ensure the motherboard metal heatsink cover is screwed down firmly over the drive.

fix_steps.title: Peel plastic protective cover off SSD heatsink thermal pad
fix_steps.detail: Motherboard heatsinks come with blue or pink thermal pads covered by clear plastic film. Peel off the film before screwing the heatsink down.

fix_steps.title: Move SSD away from graphics card exhaust
fix_steps.detail: If your primary M.2 slot sits directly underneath the GPU PCIe slot where hot exhaust dumps, install the SSD in an alternate CPU-connected slot with a dedicated heatsink.

fix_steps.title: Ensure adequate front case intake airflow
fix_steps.detail: Verify front intake case fans blow fresh ambient air directly across the lower motherboard surface.

title: Tangled loose cables obstructing front case fan airflow
summary: A rat's nest of loose PSU cables and drives directly behind front intake fans obstructs laminar air paths to the CPU and graphics card.
symptoms: Front case fans make buzzing or whooshing noise against loose wires
No measurable air movement felt near GPU intake fans
Ambient internal case temperature is 10-15°C warmer than room temperature

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Route power cables through rear motherboard tray grommets
fix_steps.detail: Unplug modular cables and tuck them behind the rear motherboard tray. Use zip-ties or velcro straps to bind them flat against chassis tie-down loops.

fix_steps.title: Tuck unused non-modular PSU cables into the bottom shroud
fix_steps.detail: Stuff surplus cables into the empty drive cage space inside the bottom PSU tunnel away from the path of front intake fans.

fix_steps.title: Relocate 3.5" mechanical drive bays
fix_steps.detail: If you don't use 3.5" hard drives, unbolt the modular drive cage situated in front of the bottom front fan to open an unrestricted air tunnel to the GPU.

fix_steps.title: Verify no cables touch spinning fan blades
fix_steps.detail: Ensure slim PWM or RGB wires are tied down so they cannot migrate into spinning fan blades.

title: GDDR6X VRAM memory junction overheating (105C - 110C thermal throttle)
summary: Micron GDDR6X memory modules on high-end graphics cards (RTX 3080/3090/4080/4090) reach critical junction limits due to deteriorated, oily, or poorly compressed factory thermal pads.
symptoms: HWInfo64 reports 'Memory Temperature' or 'GPU Memory Junction' pegged at 106C - 110C
Games stutter violently after 10 minutes as GPU core clocks down to protect memory
GPU core temp is cool (65C) but GPU fans spin at 100% emergency speed

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Monitor GPU Memory Junction Temperature in HWInfo64
fix_steps.detail: Download HWInfo64, launch in Sensors-only mode, launch a demanding game, and observe 'GPU Memory Junction Temperature'. Maximum operating limit before thermal throttling is 105C.

fix_steps.title: Cap in-game framerates and lower memory intensive settings
fix_steps.detail: Cap your framerate to your monitor refresh rate (e.g. 144 FPS) using NVIDIA Control Panel Max Frame Rate, and lower Ray Tracing and texture resolution to reduce VRAM bus utilization.

fix_steps.title: Add an intake fan blowing directly across GPU backplate
fix_steps.detail: Position a 120mm bottom or side chassis fan pushing fresh cool air directly across the graphics card rear backplate to pull heat away from rear-mounted VRAM packages.

fix_steps.title: Replace factory VRAM thermal pads with high-performance pads
fix_steps.detail: Disassemble the GPU heatsink and replace oily stock thermal pads with high-conductivity pads (like Gelid GP-Ultimate or Thermalright Odyssey) with the exact millimeter thickness specified for your GPU model.

title: AIO liquid cooler gurgling noise and high CPU temps from pump orientation
summary: Air bubbles migrate into the AIO CPU water block pump impeller because the radiator is mounted with the pump at the highest physical point in the liquid loop.
symptoms: Audible bubbling, clicking, or rattling noise originating from the CPU pump block
CPU idle temperatures jump from 40C up to 75C without running any software
Radiator tubes are mounted below the CPU block level

fix_steps.title: Ensure top of radiator is higher than the CPU pump block
fix_steps.detail: Inspect your case layout. The top of the radiator (or radiator tank) MUST sit physically higher than the CPU water block so air bubbles naturally pool in the top of the radiator away from the pump.

fix_steps.title: Tilt PC chassis while pump is running to dislodge air
fix_steps.detail: Power on the PC, set pump speed to 100% in BIOS, and gently tilt the computer chassis backward and forward by 45 degrees to force trapped air bubbles up the tubing and into the radiator.

fix_steps.title: Remount radiator to the top chassis exhaust position
fix_steps.detail: If the radiator is currently mounted at the bottom of the case, move it to the top roof panel as exhaust. Top mounting is the gold standard for zero air ingestion.

fix_steps.title: Set AIO pump header speed to constant 100% / Full Speed in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: In BIOS hardware monitor, select the pump header (AIO_PUMP or W_PUMP) and set it to a constant 100% DC/PWM duty cycle. Liquid pumps are engineered to run at constant RPM, not variable fan curves.

title: Gaming laptop thermal throttling on bed, couch, or soft blanket
summary: Soft fabrics compress against bottom chassis intake grilles, completely choking fan airflow and causing the CPU and GPU to thermal throttle down to minimum frequencies.
symptoms: Laptop chassis feels burning hot to touch above the keyboard deck
Massive FPS drops and stuttering when gaming from bed or sofa
Fans scream at maximum RPM but exhaust vents push out minimal airflow

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Place laptop on a hard, flat, rigid surface
fix_steps.detail: Always operate gaming laptops on a desk, wooden lap desk, or hard tray. Soft bedding compresses under the rubber feet and blocks the bottom intake vents completely.

fix_steps.title: Elevate the rear laptop feet by 1-2 inches
fix_steps.detail: Prop the rear rubber feet of the laptop up by one inch using small rubber stands, bottle caps, or an angled stand. This lowers CPU and GPU temperatures by 5C to 8C by doubling intake air volume.

fix_steps.title: Clean lint and pet hair from internal heatsink fins
fix_steps.detail: Laptops used on beds ingest high volumes of blanket fibers and dust. Remove the bottom chassis cover and use compressed air to blast lint out through the copper exhaust fins. SAFETY: Hold the fan blades still with a finger or non-conductive tool while spraying compressed air. Allowing fans to free-spin rapidly can burn out bearings and generate reverse voltage back into the motherboard fan header.

fix_steps.title: Invest in a pressurized laptop cooling pad (IETS / Llano)
fix_steps.detail: High-performance sealed-foam cooling pads force filtered air into the laptop chassis under positive pressure, dramatically reducing temperatures in thin chassis.

title: Motherboard case fans stuck at 100% speed (jet engine noise)
summary: PWM 4-pin fans are configured in legacy DC Voltage mode in the BIOS, feeding a constant 12V rail that forces the fan motors to run at maximum RPM non-stop.
symptoms: Case fans scream at maximum RPM immediately upon booting into Windows
Adjusting fan curves in Windows software has zero effect on fan noise
Fan noise is deafening even when CPU temperature is at cool 30C idle

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Switch fan header mode from DC to PWM in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Restart PC and tap Del to enter BIOS. Open Q-Fan / Smart Fan / Hardware Monitor. Locate each fan header (CHA_FAN, SYS_FAN) and change control mode from 'DC' to 'PWM'.

fix_steps.title: Verify 4-pin PWM fan header connection
fix_steps.detail: Check the fan cable header on the motherboard. Ensure 4-pin PWM fans are plugged into all 4 pins and not misaligned across 3 pins on the connector.

fix_steps.title: Install Fan Control open-source software
fix_steps.detail: Download free open-source 'Fan Control' by Rem0o. Run the setup wizard to detect all motherboard and GPU sensors and create quiet custom stepped fan curves.

fix_steps.title: Check CPU temperature sensor readout in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: If BIOS reads CPU temp as 99C while the heatsink is cold, the temperature probe is uncalibrated or disconnected, forcing safety failsafe 100% fan speed.

title: Damaged CPU heatsink heatpipe loss of vacuum causing instant 100C spike
summary: A punctured, cracked, or severely bent sintered copper heatpipe loses its internal partial vacuum, terminating the liquid phase-change cycle and dropping thermal conductivity to near zero.
symptoms: CPU spikes to 100C within 3 seconds of launching any game or benchmark
CPU cooler aluminum fins remain cold to the touch while CPU core is thermal throttling
Heatsink was dropped, bent, or damaged during shipping or moving

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Perform touch test on cooler heatpipes and fin stack
fix_steps.detail: When the CPU reports 95C-100C under load, touch the top of the aluminum cooling fins. If the heatpipes and fins feel room temperature while the CPU throttles, heat is not transferring through the pipes.

fix_steps.title: Inspect copper heatpipe tips for cracks or punctures
fix_steps.detail: Examine the sealed ends of the copper heatpipes at the top of the cooler tower. If a seal is crimped open or punctured, the internal distilled water vapor has escaped.

fix_steps.title: Verify thermal paste footprint and mounting pressure first
fix_steps.detail: Remove the cooler and verify the thermal paste was evenly squished into a paper-thin layer. Rule out a missed plastic peel sticker before condemning the heatsink.

fix_steps.title: Replace the damaged CPU cooler tower
fix_steps.detail: A heatpipe with loss of vacuum cannot be repaired or refilled. Replace the cooler with a budget modern dual-tower air cooler (like Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120).

title: Power supply hybrid eco mode overheating inside enclosed PSU shroud
summary: The power supply zero-RPM fan mode keeps the internal fan motionless until 50% power load, allowing heat to soak into internal capacitors inside cases with solid unventilated PSU shrouds.
symptoms: Case basement / PSU shroud feels extremely hot to the touch during gaming
PC shuts down abruptly without blue screen after 30-45 minutes of heavy load
Power supply fan only spins for 10 seconds right before the emergency thermal trip

fix_steps.title: Toggle off the ECO / Semi-Passive / Hybrid switch on the PSU
fix_steps.detail: Locate the small push-button or rocker switch on the back of the PSU labeled 'Eco Mode', 'Hybrid', or 'Smart Fan'. Switch it to OFF so the cooling fan runs continuously at quiet low RPM.

fix_steps.title: Verify PSU fan intake orientation (pointing downward)
fix_steps.detail: Check the power supply installation orientation. The large fan grille should face DOWNWARD toward the bottom case dust filter to draw fresh ambient air from under the chassis.

fix_steps.title: Clean bottom chassis power supply dust filter
fix_steps.detail: Slide out the mesh dust filter from under the rear bottom of your PC case. Wash out accumulated carpet lint and dust with warm water, dry thoroughly, and reinsert.

fix_steps.title: Never place PC tower directly on plush carpet
fix_steps.detail: Plush carpets sink under case feet, completely sealing off the bottom power supply air intake. Place a flat wooden board, acrylic sheet, or PC stand under the tower.

title: PCIe 4.0 / 5.0 NVMe SSD thermal throttling without motherboard heatsink
summary: High-speed PCIe Gen 4 and Gen 5 NVMe SSD controllers draw up to 8-11W under continuous write operations, overheating to 85C and throttling read/write speeds from 7,000 MB/s down to 250 MB/s.
symptoms: Steam or Epic Games download freezes and disk usage drops to 0 MB/s periodically
HWInfo64 or CrystalDiskInfo shows Drive Temperature 2 (Controller) exceeding 85C - 90C
Large file transfers start at 5 GB/s and drop to a crawl within 15 seconds

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Install motherboard metal M.2 thermal armor heatsink
fix_steps.detail: Never run high-speed PCIe Gen 4/5 SSDs bare. Install the thick aluminum heatsink shield that came with your motherboard, ensuring the blue protective plastic film is peeled from the thermal pad.

fix_steps.title: Monitor Drive Temperature 2 (ASIC Controller) in HWInfo64
fix_steps.detail: Drive Temp 1 reports NAND flash memory (which likes running warm around 40-60C), while Drive Temp 2 reports the controller. The controller must stay below 80C to prevent thermal throttling.

fix_steps.title: Add third-party M.2 copper fin heatsink
fix_steps.detail: If your motherboard lacks integrated M.2 heatsinks, install an aftermarket $10 copper fin heatsink (like Thermalright HR-09 or be quiet! MC1) with dual-sided thermal pads.

fix_steps.title: Move M.2 SSD away from directly under hot GPU exhaust
fix_steps.detail: If using secondary slots, avoid placing bare M.2 drives directly underneath a 300W graphics card exhaust port where heat soak drives SSD temperatures past safety thresholds.

title: Laptop thermal paste pump-out degradation (degraded cooling after 2 months)
summary: Traditional silicone-based thermal paste on bare-die laptop processors squishes out from thermal expansion and contraction cycles (the pump-out effect), leading to dry-out and thermal throttling.
symptoms: Laptop temperatures were great right after repasting, but spiked back to 95C+ within 8-12 weeks
Core-to-core temperature deltas exceed 15C-20C under load
Disassembly reveals thermal paste pushed out around die edges with bare center silicon

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Replace standard paste with Honeywell PTM7950 phase-change pad
fix_steps.detail: Standard paste (MX-4, Kryonaut) pumps out quickly on bare silicon dies. Order genuine Honeywell PTM7950 phase-change pad; it is solid at room temperature and melts under heat, completely eliminating pump-out.

fix_steps.title: Pre-chill PTM7950 in refrigerator before cutting
fix_steps.detail: Place the PTM7950 sheet in the fridge for 10 minutes to make it stiff. Cut exactly to the size of the CPU and GPU dies, peel the plastic liner, apply to the die, and screw down the heatsink.

fix_steps.title: Use high-viscosity viscous paste if PTM is unavailable
fix_steps.detail: If you must use paste, use high-viscosity thick compounds designed for direct-die applications (like Thermalright TFX, Gelid GC-Extreme, or K5 Pro on memory modules).

fix_steps.title: Tighten laptop heatsink screws in numbered sequence
fix_steps.detail: Laptop copper vapor chambers have numbered screw posts (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Always tighten them strictly in ascending sequence to prevent tilting the contact plate and pinching paste to one side.

title: PC case and CPU fans revving up and down loudly every 5 seconds
summary: Fans repeatedly accelerate to 100% and drop back down during light desktop usage, causing annoying fan oscillation.
symptoms: Fans ramp up to high RPM when opening a browser tab and spin down immediately
Audible pulsating fan noise every few seconds
Modern Ryzen and Intel CPUs spiking to 65C for 1 second during background tasks

fix_steps.title: Add Fan Step Up / Step Down time delay (Hysteresis) in BIOS
fix_steps.instruction: Reboot into BIOS -> open Hardware Monitor / Q-Fan Control / Smart Fan. Find 'CPU Fan Step Up Time' (or Spin Up Time) and set to '3.0 seconds' (or Level 3). Set 'Step Down Time' to '5.0 seconds'.
fix_steps.caution: This delays fan response so short 1-second temperature spikes do not trigger sudden fan revving.
fix_steps.detail: Reboot into BIOS -> open Hardware Monitor / Q-Fan Control / Smart Fan. Find 'CPU Fan Step Up Time' (or Spin Up Time) and set to '3.0 seconds' (or Level 3). Set 'Step Down Time' to '5.0 seconds'.

fix_steps.title: Flatten the fan curve below 65 degrees Celsius
fix_steps.instruction: In the BIOS fan curve graph, keep fan speed at a constant quiet 35% to 40% from 30C up to 65C. Only ramp up fan speed when temperatures exceed 75C under actual gaming or render workloads.
fix_steps.caution: Modern 7nm/5nm CPUs run hot at idle by design; constant 40% fan speed is completely safe.
fix_steps.detail: In the BIOS fan curve graph, keep fan speed at a constant quiet 35% to 40% from 30C up to 65C. Only ramp up fan speed when temperatures exceed 75C under actual gaming or render workloads.

fix_steps.title: Use Fan Control software to sync case fans to GPU temperature
fix_steps.instruction: Download free open-source 'Fan Control' (by Rem0o). Set front intake case fans to follow GPU temperature instead of CPU spikes for whisper-quiet desktop operation.
fix_steps.caution: Save configuration and enable 'Start with Windows'.
fix_steps.detail: Download free open-source 'Fan Control' (by Rem0o). Set front intake case fans to follow GPU temperature instead of CPU spikes for whisper-quiet desktop operation.

title: Liquid AIO cooler CPU temperature hitting 95C-100C at idle (Pump Failure)
summary: CPU temperatures instantly spike to 100C within 60 seconds of turning on PC, fans spin at maximum, and PC shuts down.
symptoms: CPU temperature reaches 90C-100C at idle in BIOS or desktop
AIO radiator fans blowing cool air while CPU is burning hot
BIOS reports 'CPU Fan Error' or AIO pump RPM reads 0 RPM

fix_steps.title: Check AIO pump power connector and RPM in BIOS
fix_steps.instruction: Check that the 3-pin or 4-pin AIO pump header is plugged into the motherboard's dedicated 'AIO_PUMP' or 'W_PUMP' port (set to 100% full speed in BIOS). Verify pump reads between 2000-4500 RPM.
fix_steps.caution: Never plug an AIO pump into a port set to low DC voltage control.
fix_steps.detail: Check that the 3-pin or 4-pin AIO pump header is plugged into the motherboard's dedicated 'AIO_PUMP' or 'W_PUMP' port (set to 100% full speed in BIOS). Verify pump reads between 2000-4500 RPM.

fix_steps.title: Feel both rubber coolant tubes for vibration and temperature disparity
fix_steps.instruction: Gently touch both rubber tubes with fingers. You should feel slight fluid vibration. If one tube is scorching hot and the other tube is stone cold, coolant is not circulating (pump impeller is stuck or dead).
fix_steps.caution: Do not pull on the tubes; simply touch the exterior sleeve.
fix_steps.detail: Gently touch both rubber tubes with fingers. You should feel slight fluid vibration. If one tube is scorching hot and the other tube is stone cold, coolant is not circulating (pump impeller is stuck or dead).

fix_steps.title: Check AIO radiator orientation for trapped air bubbles
fix_steps.instruction: Ensure the highest point of the AIO radiator loop is ABOVE the CPU block. If the radiator is mounted at the bottom of the case, air bubbles rise into the pump, running it dry and burning it out.
fix_steps.caution: Mount radiator to the top of the case (preferred) or front with tubes at the bottom.
fix_steps.detail: Ensure the highest point of the AIO radiator loop is ABOVE the CPU block. If the radiator is mounted at the bottom of the case, air bubbles rise into the pump, running it dry and burning it out.

title: CPU cooler plastic protective peel was left on the copper coldplate
summary: Newly built PC throttles at 90C-100C immediately because the transparent factory peel sticker was not removed before applying paste.
symptoms: Brand new PC build reaches 95C-100C under light load or Cinebench test
Cooler is properly screwed down and fans spin, but thermals are terrible
Thermal paste was applied directly on top of the factory plastic warning film

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Remove CPU cooler and inspect coldplate base
fix_steps.instruction: Unscrew CPU cooler mounting bracket. Lift cooler straight up. Check the bottom copper surface. Look for a transparent plastic film with warning text ('Warning! Please peel off before installation').
fix_steps.caution: On AMD AM4/AM5 CPUs, twist cooler gently back and forth before pulling up so CPU does not get pulled out of socket.
fix_steps.detail: Unscrew CPU cooler mounting bracket. gently twist the cooler left and right to break the thermal paste seal before lifting. Check the bottom copper surface. Look for a transparent plastic film with warning text ('Warning! Please peel off before installation').

fix_steps.title: Peel off plastic sticker and clean surfaces with isopropyl alcohol
fix_steps.instruction: Peel off the plastic film completely. Clean old thermal paste off both the CPU heat spreader and cooler copper base using 90%+ Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) and a lint-free coffee filter or paper towel.
fix_steps.caution: Ensure copper base is completely clean and dry before applying new paste.
fix_steps.detail: Peel off the plastic film completely. Clean old thermal paste off both the CPU heat spreader and cooler copper base using 90%+ Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) and a lint-free coffee filter or paper towel.

fix_steps.title: Apply fresh pea-sized drop of thermal paste and remount
fix_steps.instruction: Place a pea-sized dot of quality thermal paste (Arctic MX-4/MX-6, Noctua NT-H1, Thermalright TF7) in the center of the CPU. Re-tighten cooler screws in a criss-cross X pattern until snug.
fix_steps.caution: Do not over-tighten; stop when screws reach natural resistance.
fix_steps.detail: Place a pea-sized dot of quality thermal paste (Arctic MX-4/MX-6, Noctua NT-H1, Thermalright TF7) in the center of the CPU. Re-tighten cooler screws in a criss-cross X pattern until snug.

title: Laptop CPU/GPU overheating again 2 weeks after repasting (Thermal Paste Pump-Out)
summary: Repasted gaming laptop with thermal paste, but temperatures spike to 95C again after a few days.
symptoms: Fresh thermal paste worked great for 1 week then CPU temps spiked to 95C-100C
Opening laptop shows bare silicon die in the center with paste pushed to the outer edges
Direct-die mobile silicon with low mounting pressure suffers from pump-out effect

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Replace standard silicone paste with Honeywell PTM7950 Phase Change Material
fix_steps.instruction: Laptops lack the heavy metal heat spreader (IHS) of desktop CPUs and have low spring mounting pressure. Traditional thermal paste pumps out due to thermal expansion cycles. Apply Honeywell PTM7950 (0.2mm phase-change thermal pad) cut to exact die dimensions.
fix_steps.caution: Freeze PTM7950 in freezer for 10 minutes before peeling the plastic backing to make application easy.
fix_steps.detail: Laptops lack the heavy metal heat spreader (IHS) of desktop CPUs and have low spring mounting pressure. Traditional thermal paste pumps out due to thermal expansion cycles. Apply Honeywell PTM7950 (0.2mm phase-change thermal pad) cut to exact die dimensions.

fix_steps.title: Check thermal putty on VRMs and VRAM chips
fix_steps.instruction: Do NOT use thick thermal pads on laptop VRMs/VRAM if factory used thermal paste/putty. Thick pads prevent heatsink from making contact with CPU die. Use high-performance thermal putty (e.g. Upsiren U6 Pro or K5 Pro).
fix_steps.caution: Ensure heatsink sits perfectly flat and parallel on CPU and GPU dies.
fix_steps.detail: Do NOT use thick thermal pads on laptop VRMs/VRAM if factory used thermal paste/putty. Thick pads prevent heatsink from making contact with CPU die. Use high-performance thermal putty (e.g. Upsiren U6 Pro or K5 Pro).

fix_steps.title: Tighten heatsink screws in strict numbered sequence (1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4)
fix_steps.instruction: Laptop heatsinks have small numbers stamped near each screw hole (1 through 6 or 8). Tighten each screw halfway in numerical order, then do a second pass tightening them fully.
fix_steps.caution: Prevents cracking the bare silicon corners or creating uneven contact pressure.
fix_steps.detail: Laptop heatsinks have small numbers stamped near each screw hole (1 through 6 or 8). Tighten each screw halfway in numerical order, then do a second pass tightening them fully.

title: GPU Hotspot / Junction temperature reaching 105C while Core temperature is only 70C
summary: HWiNFO shows a 35C delta between GPU Core and GPU Hotspot, causing fans to scream at 100% emergency speed.
symptoms: GPU core reports 68C-72C, but GPU Hotspot / Memory Junction reaches 105C-110C
Fans violently spike to 100% (3500 RPM) while playing demanding games
GPU throttles clock speed down by 300MHz to prevent thermal breakdown

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Check GPU mounting screw torque on the back retention bracket
fix_steps.instruction: The X-bracket or 4 spring screws behind the GPU core provide mounting pressure. If screws loosened over time, heatsink loses contact with the silicon center. Gently snug down the 4 center spring screws in an X-pattern.
fix_steps.caution: Do not force screws past their stop point.
fix_steps.detail: The X-bracket or 4 spring screws behind the GPU core provide mounting pressure. If screws loosened over time, heatsink loses contact with the silicon center. Gently snug down the 4 center spring screws in an X-pattern.

fix_steps.title: Repaste GPU with viscous, non-pumpout thermal paste
fix_steps.instruction: If the delta between core and hotspot is greater than 20C, thermal paste has dried out or pumped out. Disassemble GPU cooler, clean with 99% IPA, and apply a thick viscous paste (Gelid GC-Extreme, Thermal Grizzly Kryonaut Extreme, or PTM7950).
fix_steps.caution: Fully spread the paste manually across 100% of the bare GPU die; do not rely on pea-dot method on bare silicon.
fix_steps.detail: If the delta between core and hotspot is greater than 20C, thermal paste has dried out or pumped out. Disassemble GPU cooler, clean with 99% IPA, and apply a thick viscous paste (Gelid GC-Extreme, Thermal Grizzly Kryonaut Extreme, or PTM7950).

fix_steps.title: Apply GPU undervolt in MSI Afterburner
fix_steps.instruction: Press Ctrl+F in MSI Afterburner to open the voltage/frequency curve editor. Flatten the curve at 900mV (0.900V) at your stock boost clock. This reduces GPU power consumption by 50-80W with zero loss in FPS, dropping hotspot temps by 15C.
fix_steps.caution: Test stability with 20 loops of 3DMark Time Spy or Unigine Superposition.

title: Thick 'dust felt' blanket clogging heatsink fins and radiator interior
summary: Fans spin at full speed but no air comes out of the exhaust vents due to compacted dust mat inside cooling fins.
symptoms: Fans are screaming loudly, but placing your hand behind exhaust vents reveals almost zero airflow
PC or laptop gradually became 20C hotter over 1-2 years of use
Dust has formed a solid felt-like mat between fan blades and radiator fins

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Hold fan blades still while blowing compressed air
fix_steps.instruction: CRITICAL: Hold fan blades with a pencil or finger so they cannot spin when using compressed air. Blowing air on free-spinning fans can over-spin bearings and generate reverse electrical current into the motherboard fan header.
fix_steps.caution: CRITICAL: Never let fans spin freely at high RPM from compressed air.
fix_steps.detail: CRITICAL: Hold fan blades with a pencil or finger so they cannot spin when using compressed air. Blowing air on free-spinning fans can over-spin bearings and generate reverse electrical current into the motherboard fan header.

fix_steps.title: Blow air opposite the normal airflow direction
fix_steps.instruction: To dislodge the compacted dust blanket, blow compressed air from the outside exhaust vents BACKWARDS toward the fan intake. The solid dust mat will pop off the fins intact for easy removal with tweezers.
fix_steps.caution: Do this outdoors or in a garage to avoid inhaling fine dust particles.
fix_steps.detail: To dislodge the compacted dust blanket, blow compressed air from the outside exhaust vents BACKWARDS toward the fan intake. The solid dust mat will pop off the fins intact for easy removal with tweezers. SAFETY: Hold the fan blades still with a finger or non-conductive tool while spraying compressed air. Allowing fans to free-spin rapidly can burn out bearings and generate reverse voltage back into the motherboard fan header.

fix_steps.title: Clean magnetic case dust filters with warm water
fix_steps.instruction: Remove front and bottom PSU mesh dust filters. Wash under warm tap water, dry completely with a towel for 30 minutes, and reinstall. Clean filters restore 100% fresh air intake to GPU and CPU.
fix_steps.caution: Ensure mesh filters are 100% dry before putting them back near electronics.
fix_steps.detail: Remove front and bottom PSU mesh dust filters. Wash under warm tap water, dry completely with a towel for 30 minutes, and reinstall. Clean filters restore 100% fresh air intake to GPU and CPU.

title: CPU TjMax Thermal Shutdown and PROCHOT Throttling Triage
summary: Diagnose processor thermal throttling at Intel/AMD TjMax temperature boundaries (100C-105C) and emergency PROCHOT hardware thermal shutdowns.
symptoms: CPU clock frequencies drop dramatically from 5GHz down to 800MHz under load
PC powers off abruptly without blue screen dump when reaching 100C-115C temperatures
HWInfo64 shows red flags on Core Thermal Throttling or PROCHOT EXT / CPU

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Monitor per-core temperatures and PROCHOT in HWInfo64
fix_steps.detail: Launch HWInfo64 in Sensors-only mode, run Cinebench or game, and watch Core Max and PROCHOT flags. Intel chips throttle at 100C-105C; AMD Zen 4/5 chips throttle at 95C. Shutoff occurs at roughly 115C.

fix_steps.title: Verify cooler peel sticker was removed
fix_steps.detail: A transparent plastic peel sticker left on the copper cold plate of the CPU cooler prevents direct heat transfer. Warm up CPU with a brief workload beforehand, then gently twist cooler left and right to break thermal paste vacuum before removing. Inspect base, peel plastic film if present, clean, and repaste.

fix_steps.title: Check cooler mounting standoff torque and backplate
fix_steps.detail: Uneven mounting pressure causes poor thermal contact. Ensure LGA1700 or AM4/AM5 standoffs are screwed down completely and cooler retention screws are tightened diagonally in criss-cross pattern until hand-tight.

fix_steps.title: Apply high-quality non-conductive thermal paste
fix_steps.detail: Clean old paste with 99% isopropyl alcohol. Apply a pea-sized dot or thin X pattern of quality thermal paste (Noctua NT-H2, Thermal Grizzly Kryonaut, Arctic MX-6) across the integrated heat spreader (IHS).

title: GPU Hotspot Junction Temperature Limit and Shutoff Triage
summary: Troubleshoot GPU thermal emergency shutdowns triggered when GPU Hotspot (Junction) temperature hits 105C-110C while average core temperature appears normal.
symptoms: GPU fans suddenly scream at 100% maximum RPM while gaming
Display goes black while game audio continues playing in background
HWInfo64 reports GPU Core at 72C while GPU Hotspot is at 105C (delta exceeding 30C)

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Monitor GPU Core and Hotspot delta simultaneously
fix_steps.detail: In HWInfo64, observe GPU Temperature and GPU Hotspot Temperature under 3D load. A normal delta is 10C to 15C. A delta exceeding 25C indicates thermal paste pump-out or uneven heatsink contact.

fix_steps.title: Inspect rear X-bracket retention screws
fix_steps.detail: Check the four spring-loaded screws securing the heatsink to the GPU core on the backplate. Gently tighten each screw diagonally half a turn at a time to equalize mounting pressure.

fix_steps.title: Repaste GPU die with phase-change PTM7950 pad
fix_steps.detail: Direct-die bare silicon GPUs pump out standard thermal paste within weeks. Disassemble heatsink, clean die, and apply Honeywell PTM7950 phase-change pad or high-viscosity paste (Thermal Grizzly Aeronaut/Kryonaut Extreme).

fix_steps.title: Replace degraded VRAM thermal pads
fix_steps.detail: Inspect GDDR6/GDDR6X thermal pads for oil weeping or tearing. Replace with precise manufacturer-thickness pads (usually 1.0mm, 1.5mm, or 2.0mm) to prevent pad thickness from lifting the cold plate off the core.

title: BIOS Fan Curve Hysteresis and PWM vs DC Header Optimization
summary: Eliminate annoying fan revving loops every few seconds by configuring temperature smoothing hysteresis and setting proper 4-pin PWM header modes.
symptoms: CPU and chassis fans ramp loudly to 100% then drop back down every 5 to 10 seconds
Fans make annoying pulsing noises during light tasks like opening browser tabs
Case fans spin at maximum speed constantly despite low system temperatures

fix_steps.title: Enter motherboard BIOS fan control interface
fix_steps.detail: Restart computer and press Del or F2 during boot. Navigate to Hardware Monitor / Fan Control (ASUS Q-Fan, MSI Smart Fan, Gigabyte Smart Fan 6, ASRock Fan-Tastic).

fix_steps.title: Verify PWM vs DC header mode for each fan
fix_steps.detail: For 4-pin fans, ensure header control mode is set to PWM (Pulse Width Modulation). Setting a 4-pin fan to DC (Voltage) mode can cause erratic RPM control or run at 100% full speed.

fix_steps.title: Configure fan step-up and step-down hysteresis delay
fix_steps.detail: Locate Fan Step Up / Step Down time (or Temperature Interval / Smoothing). Set step-up delay to 2-3 seconds and step-down delay to 3-5 seconds so brief 1-second CPU temperature spikes do not trigger fan ramp-ups.

fix_steps.title: Tune flat baseline curve up to 65C
fix_steps.detail: Set fan curve to hold quiet 35%-40% RPM flatly until CPU temperature reaches 65C, then gradually ramp up to 75% at 80C, and 100% at 85C.

title: AIO Liquid Cooler Pump Header Constant Speed Configuration
summary: Configure dedicated AIO_PUMP and W_PUMP motherboard headers to constant 100% speed to prevent liquid coolant stalling, cavitation, and overheating.
symptoms: AIO cooler tubes feel hot near CPU block while radiator remains completely cold
CPU idles at 60C-75C and throttles instantly under any small load
Liquid cooler pump makes clicking, gurgling, or buzzing noises

fix_steps.title: Verify pump tachometer header connection
fix_steps.detail: Inspect physical wiring inside chassis. The 3-pin or 4-pin cable running from the AIO pump block should be connected to the dedicated AIO_PUMP or W_PUMP header on the motherboard, not standard CPU_FAN.

fix_steps.title: Set AIO_PUMP header to 100% constant full speed in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Enter BIOS setup -> Fan Monitor. Select AIO_PUMP / W_PUMP header, change control mode to Full Speed or 100% duty cycle, and disable temperature curve regulation. Liquid pumps require constant 12V voltage to maintain coolant flow.

fix_steps.title: Connect radiator fans to CPU_FAN header
fix_steps.detail: Connect the radiator cooling fans to CPU_FAN (and CPU_OPT if multiple fans). This ensures fan RPM ramps up and down dynamically based on CPU temperature while pump flow remains steady.

fix_steps.title: Tilt chassis to dislodge air bubbles
fix_steps.detail: If gurgling or cavitation sounds persist, tilt the PC chassis gently while running so trapped air bubbles migrate out of the pump block up into the radiator reservoir.

title: GPU Microsecond Transient Power Spike and PSU OCP Tripping Triage
summary: Diagnose instant PC shutdowns during intense gaming caused by modern high-end GPU microsecond transient power spikes tripping PSU Over Current Protection.
symptoms: PC powers off instantly during sudden gameplay transitions (launching game, explosion, loading screen)
No blue screen dump is created; power supply requires flipping AC rocker switch off and on to restart
System runs fine under synthetic CPU stress tests but shuts off immediately in games

fix_steps.title: Identify GPU transient power spikes
fix_steps.detail: Modern graphics cards (RTX 3080/3090/4080/4090 and RX 6900/7900 series) generate microsecond transient load spikes drawing 2x to 3x their rated TDP, triggering Over Current Protection (OCP) or Over Power Protection (OPP) on older ATX 2.4 power supplies.

fix_steps.title: Ensure independent PCIe 8-pin cables
fix_steps.detail: Do not use daisy-chained pigtail cables. Each 8-pin power socket on the GPU must have its own dedicated cable running directly to a separate output port on the modular PSU. CRITICAL SAFETY: Only use modular cables designed specifically for your exact power supply model. Modular PSU pinouts are not standardized across manufacturers; mixing cables can deliver reverse polarity and immediately destroy components.

fix_steps.title: Test with GPU power limit reduced to 80%
fix_steps.detail: Open MSI Afterburner, reduce Power Limit slider to 80%, and test gaming load. If shutdowns cease completely, transient power excursions tripping PSU protections are confirmed.

fix_steps.title: Upgrade to ATX 3.0 / PCIe 5.0 compliant power supply
fix_steps.detail: ATX 3.0 compliant power supplies are engineered to withstand up to 200% excursion power spikes for 100 microseconds without tripping protection circuits.

title: Dedicated PCIe 8-Pin Cables vs Daisy-Chain Pigtails Triage
summary: Prevent 12V rail voltage droop, connector overheating, and stability crashes by using separate dedicated PCIe 8-pin power cables for high-wattage graphics cards.
symptoms: Graphics card crashes or display driver resets under 3D load
PCIe power connector or cable feels uncomfortably hot to the touch near GPU
HWInfo64 reports GPU 12V PCIe input voltage dropping below 11.4V under load

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Inspect GPU power cabling setup
fix_steps.detail: Examine the cables connected to your graphics card. If a single cable from the power supply branches into two 6+2 pin connectors plugged into the GPU, this is a daisy-chained pigtail configuration.

fix_steps.title: Understand 8-pin PCIe power delivery limits
fix_steps.detail: A standard 8-pin PCIe connector is rated for 150W; the motherboard PCIe slot provides 75W. For GPUs drawing over 225W, drawing 300W through a single 18AWG wire run causes significant resistance, heat, and voltage droop.

fix_steps.title: Run separate dedicated PCIe cables from PSU
fix_steps.detail: Plug additional independent PCIe 8-pin cables into your modular power supply and connect one dedicated cable to each socket on the graphics card. CRITICAL SAFETY: Only use modular cables designed specifically for your exact power supply model. Modular PSU pinouts are not standardized across manufacturers; mixing cables can deliver reverse polarity and immediately destroy components.

fix_steps.title: Monitor 12V input voltage under load
fix_steps.detail: Launch HWInfo64, start a 3D gaming workload, and monitor GPU 12V Input Voltage. The reading should remain firmly between 11.8V and 12.2V.
